title: Non-Animal Methods
summary: The tests that replace animals are not hypothetical. Most are adopted OECD Test Guidelines, internationally accepted for regulatory submission. This is what the science actually looks like, endpoint by endpoint.

framing.title: The 3Rs
framing.body: The framework underlying all of this was published in 1959 by William Russell and Rex Burch in The Principles of Humane Experimental Technique: Replacement of animals with alternatives, Reduction in the number used, and Refinement of procedures to lessen suffering. Regulatory science has spent six decades moving from Refinement toward Replacement. Cosmetics is the sector where Replacement has advanced furthest, because the law forced it to.

guidelines.name: In vitro skin corrosion: reconstructed human epidermis (RhE) test method
In vitro skin corrosion: transcutaneous electrical resistance test (TER)
In vitro membrane barrier test method for skin corrosion

endpoints.how: A three-dimensional model of human epidermis, grown from donated human keratinocytes, is exposed to the substance. Cell viability is measured. A corrosive substance kills the tissue within a defined exposure time.
endpoints.status: Full replacement. Adopted for regulatory use.

guidelines.name: In vitro skin irritation: reconstructed human epidermis test method

endpoints.how: The same reconstructed human epidermis, with a shorter exposure and a viability threshold that distinguishes irritants from non-irritants.
endpoints.status: Full replacement. Adopted for regulatory use.

endpoints.endpoint: Serious eye damage and eye irritation

guidelines.name: Reconstructed human cornea-like epithelium (RhCE) test method
Bovine corneal opacity and permeability (BCOP) test method
Isolated chicken eye test method
In vitro macromolecular test method

endpoints.how: Reconstructed human corneal tissue is the true replacement. BCOP and the isolated chicken eye use tissue recovered from animals already slaughtered for food, which reduces but does not eliminate animal use — a distinction worth keeping.
endpoints.status: Replacement for most classifications; a small number of borderline cases remain contested.

endpoints.replaces: Guinea pig maximisation test; murine local lymph node assay

guidelines.name: Direct peptide reactivity assay (DPRA) — protein binding
ARE-Nrf2 luciferase test method (KeratinoSens) — keratinocyte activation
In vitro dendritic cell activation (h-CLAT, U-SENS, IL-8 Luc assay)
Defined approaches for skin sensitisation

endpoints.how: This endpoint is the clearest demonstration of the modern approach. Rather than one animal test standing in for a whole biological process, each key event in the adverse outcome pathway — protein binding, keratinocyte activation, dendritic cell activation — is measured separately, then combined under a defined approach with a fixed data interpretation procedure.
endpoints.status: Full replacement. TG 497 provides regulatory decisions without animal data.

guidelines.name: In vitro 3T3 NRU phototoxicity test
In vitro phototoxicity: reconstructed human epidermis test method

endpoints.how: Cultured cells are exposed to the substance with and without a controlled dose of simulated sunlight. A phototoxic substance is markedly more cytotoxic under irradiation.
endpoints.status: Full replacement. One of the earliest validated replacements, accepted in the EU since 2000.

endpoints.replaces: In vivo micronucleus and comet assays

guidelines.name: Bacterial reverse mutation test (Ames test)
In vitro mammalian cell micronucleus test
In vitro mammalian cell gene mutation tests

endpoints.how: Bacterial and mammalian cell cultures are exposed and screened for mutations and chromosomal damage. For cosmetics, a positive in vitro result cannot be followed up in animals, so a negative battery is required.
endpoints.status: Full replacement in the cosmetics context, by legal necessity.

guidelines.name: Skin absorption: in vitro method

endpoints.how: Excised human or porcine skin is mounted in a diffusion cell and the substance's passage through it is measured directly. Human skin from surgical procedures gives the most relevant answer available.

guidelines.name: Exposure-led, hypothesis-driven frameworks combining in vitro bioactivity, in silico modelling, and physiologically based kinetic (PBK) models

endpoints.how: No single test replaces a repeated-dose study. Instead, an internal exposure is estimated with a PBK model, a point of departure is derived from in vitro bioactivity assays across many biological targets, and the two are compared. The SEURAT-1 and EU-ToxRisk programmes and subsequent industry case studies built this out.
endpoints.status: The hardest endpoint. Frameworks exist and have been accepted in specific cosmetic safety assessments; general regulatory acceptance across all sectors is still developing. This is where honest reporting matters most — anyone claiming this problem is fully solved is overstating it.

guidelines.code: OECD TG 249 and in vitro batteries
guidelines.name: Zebrafish embryo assays, stem cell-based embryotoxicity tests, and computational approaches

endpoints.how: Combinations of stem cell differentiation assays, embryonic model systems, and read-across from structurally similar substances with existing data.
endpoints.status: Partial. Screening and prioritisation are established; complete replacement for regulatory purposes is not yet achieved.

supporting.name: Read-across
supporting.detail: Inferring a substance's properties from structurally analogous substances with existing data. Avoids generating new animal data entirely, provided the analogue justification holds.

supporting.name: QSAR and in silico modelling
supporting.detail: Quantitative structure-activity relationship models predict toxicity from molecular structure. The OECD QSAR Toolbox is the reference implementation.

supporting.name: Adverse Outcome Pathways (AOPs)
supporting.detail: A structured description of the causal chain from a molecular initiating event to an adverse effect. AOPs are what make it possible to replace one animal test with several targeted in vitro assays.

supporting.name: Organ-on-chip and microphysiological systems
supporting.detail: Microfluidic devices supporting living human cells in tissue-like architecture with physiological flow. Promising for systemic endpoints; not yet standard in regulatory submissions.
